title: Three-competitive deterministic file migration
formal: For every finite metric space and every integer D≥1, is deterministic online file migration 3-competitive with an input-independent additive constant?
definitions: A finite metric (V,d), integer D≥1 and initial file location s∈V are known to the algorithm. For each request r_t∈V, first serve it from the current location x_(t−1), paying d(x_(t−1),r_t); then choose x_t∈V and pay D d(x_(t−1),x_t). There is exactly one file. Requests and their number are unknown in advance. An offline comparator starts at the same s, knows the entire finite request sequence and obeys the same service-then-move convention. OPT is its minimum total cost; it need not pay a final return to s. The assertion is existence of one deterministic policy for all finite metric inputs and D, with cost≤3 OPT+b(V,d,D,s) on every finite request sequence, where b is finite and independent of that sequence. Arbitrary real distances and unrestricted computation are allowed.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated proposition or its negation, for precisely the specified model.
context: The 2017 paper obtains a factor four by adaptive phase lengths. Its barrier for a restricted phase model is not a lower bound against all deterministic policies.
why: The target asks whether a canonical state-location problem reaches its known lower-bound ratio.

import_provenance.original_title: Optimal deterministic competitive ratio for file migration
import_provenance.original_statement: Is there a 3-competitive deterministic algorithm for file migration on arbitrary metric spaces, where serving a request costs its distance from the file and moving the file costs D times the distance moved? Bienkowski–Byrka–Mucha achieve ratio 4, while the general lower bound is 3.

context_blocks.text: The 2017 paper obtains a factor four by adaptive phase lengths. Its barrier for a restricted phase model is not a lower bound against all deterministic policies.

sentences: Serving a request costs its distance from the current file.
Moving the file costs D times the distance moved.
Both online and offline policies start at the same location.
The target is factor three with a sequence-independent additive constant.
The selected model uses finite metrics and integral file-size parameter D.
